sentences: **Bali** is evolving!
Once referred to as a **tropical paradise**, the island is seeing changes with **urbanization** taking over areas like **Denpasar** and **Seminyak**.
Despite this, there are still places where you can experience serenity and the island's classic beauty.
**Architectural** trends are shifting towards **modern** styles with influences beyond traditional Balinese elements.
The island now attracts those desiring modernity mixed with **tropical charm**—whether it's sleek private villas or creative, beautiful buildings.
Even with this shift, Bali manages to preserve its natural surroundings in new structures, showcasing the essence of **contemporary tropical living**.

parts.title: Serene Balinese Villas: Emerald Sunset & River

sentences: **Two villas** in Canggu highlight Balinese **architecture** and serene **landscapes** with views of rice fields.
Both Emerald Sunset and Emerald River villas blend **modern** and **traditional** styles.
Designed by Yoka Sara, the villas integrate **old ironwood poles** for structure and aesthetics.
Emerald Sunset features three buildings with a **unique metal roof**, while Emerald River is more **traditional**, with buildings around a central **"island"** of trees.
Both offer open **living spaces**, creating a relaxing holiday experience.
The interiors showcase modern comfort amid lush gardens.
Emerald Sunset includes a **living area** with a **curved roof**, while the bedroom building is complemented by a **20-meter pool**.
The villas feature elements like a **dining pavilion**, stone-tiled pool that changes colors, and breezy corridors with **inclined wooden struts**.
Guests enjoy various lounging spots, including poolside terraces and open-plan living rooms overlooking gardens.
These villas represent a perfect **holiday oasis** that mixes architecture with natural surroundings.

parts.title: Blending Homes with Landscape and Culture

paragraphs.heading: Two Homes in Harmony with Nature
sentences: **The first home** was built in **2004** as **guest quarters**.
Nestled between a **road** and a **gorge**, its design followed the **land's natural shape**.
The architects aimed to make it **blend seamlessly** into the tropical landscape.
Its standout feature is the **curved roofs**, resembling an **upside-down boat keel**, crafted to be **pre-assembled** and then reconstructed on-site in Bali.
The home consists of two interconnected buildings with striking **curved surfaces** that flow with the **land's contours**.
The **organic materials** such as wood and natural stone create an earthy feel, and the **open-plan areas** foster a light and breezy atmosphere, while blending with the surrounding **vegetation**.
**The second home** is dominated by a striking **steel framework roof**, inspired by **Frangipani tree branches**.
This frame covers a **double-storey building**, combining an open-air ground floor with enclosed upper levels, which offer seamless **garden views**.
The master bedroom's unit, initially planned with a **Frangipani motif**, ended up being a simple glass-and-wood structure.
This home exemplifies **modern tropical design** while respecting the local environment's cultural aspects.
**The house** is designed to appear as an extension of the surrounding **rice terraces**, with **natural materials** like stone and wood enhancing the feel.
The **main building** features a mix of **curved shingle roofs** and **flat stone volumes**, making it look as though it **blends into the landscape**.
Surrounded by a **curving pool** and lush **landscaping**, the house makes clever use of **varying textures** and **colors** to create a harmonious balance with its tropical setting.
A separate **guest pavilion** feels like part of the **hillside**, composed of **green Indian stone** and **bengkerai wood**.
The **roof** is artistically altered to incorporate the entrance.
The home embodies the owners' desire for **space and seclusion**, offering a tranquil retreat that stays in harmony with **Balinese aesthetics** and the beauty of the **natural environment**.

parts.title: Modernist Coastal Home with Nature-Integrated Design

sentences: In **modern home designs**, Alessandro Landi combines an open-plan living concept with dramatic **floor-to-ceiling glazing** that enhances spectacular **coastal views**.
The sleek design is balanced with raw elements like **granite** and **bamboo flooring**.
Architects like **Richard Neutra** inspire the home to mediate **man and nature**, promoting **modern living** concepts of **sun, space, and greenery**.
Though located in **Bali**, the house stands out with **international charm** rather than traditional Indonesian styles.
Inside, this modern utopia remains consistent with its exterior, utilizing **grey tones** highlighted by chromatic **red accents** such as a **bright red chaise longue**.
A **minimalist garden** and a narrow **lap pool** lined with **green sukabumi stone** frame the home, embodying an **exercise in restraint** yet designed for maximum aesthetic impact.
**Textures like Indian slate and volcanic stone** complement the clean architectural lines, while subtle lighting brings out textural intricacies during the night.
**Art from Just Jen’s**, casually placed within the living space, offers a subtle nod to Indonesian culture while maintaining overall **modernist appeal**.

parts.title: Design and Architecture of Tra Villa in Canggu

sentences: **This villa** in **Canggu** was built between 2006 **and 2007**, designed by **Yoka Sara of Bale Legend**.
The **owners initially** weren't attracted to Bali due to its commercialization.
However, they eventually fell in love with the jungle and **rice fields**, which inspired the design of **their home**.
Their vision was to always feel like they were **outside** in these natural settings.
The villa's **architecture** features **hollow steel**, **composite aluminum**, and **glass**, giving it both a modern and a natural touch.
**Ironwood columns**, used in the structure, add to its character.
The villa's design integrates with its surroundings, with views extending towards a **river** and **rice fields**.
The **landscape design** also contributes to this integration, using **local plants** such as **banana trees** and **slim palms** to enhance their **tropical living environment**.
This retreat in **Bali** was built for a dedicated surfer with spectacular **ocean views** over Padang Padang and Suluban.
Designed by David Lombardi, the house blends **indoor-outdoor living** and ensures **easy wave access**.
A main structure with shingled roof and lighter bedroom volumes incorporates a **carport** and perforated copper entrance door, showcasing local craftsmanship.
The **spacious living area** with cooling materials like palimanan stone and terrazzo floors looks out to a **minimalist landscaped** garden and pool, enhancing relaxation for any surfer.
**LEFT:** The **master bedroom** from one of the four villas at **The Calyx** showcases a sloping wooden roof and glazed windows offering ocean views.
An **impressive glass sculpture** by Seiki Torige adds an artistic touch.
The resort's **communal pool** extends over the Indian ocean; nearby, an open **bar and lounge** offer sweeping vistas, adding to the **serene atmosphere.**
The Calyx, named after a plant's **supporting part**, offers a unique retreat.
Designed by **Gfab**, the boutique resort prioritizes **energy efficiency** and blends into its landscape.
The **cream sandstone walls**, flat **plant-covered roofs**, and strategic room placements maximize natural cooling and relaxation, creating a **sequestered and modern ambience.**
The Tirtha **wedding chapels** in Bali offer a stunning backdrop for weddings.
These chapels sit on a **cliff** with breathtaking views over the **Indian Ocean**.
Designed by a **Japanese entrepreneur** and architect Glenn Parker, Tirtha Uluwatu and Tirtha Luhur combine traditional and modern elements.
The design concept includes **ivory palimanan stone** and an **A-line chapel** with glass panels and a Teflon roof, giving a sense of **lightness** and **romance**.
The architect aimed to create a dramatic, yet culturally relevant design that reflects Bali's **vernacular architecture**.
**Bamboo House**: This villa, built for Italian businessman **Kiko A Croserio**, uniquely uses **bamboo** in its construction, giving it a rustic vibe.
The house is a testament to blending traditional Indonesian materials with modern architecture.
**Bamboo** is used for poles and beams, alongside clay and wood, creating a home integrated with nature.
Perched on a tranquil site near **Tanah Lot**, the villa boasts an open-plan layout with a **free-form swimming pool** and views of the ocean.
**Wolfgang Widmoser** assisted in its design, influenced by Indonesian tradition and the legendary Frei Otto.
A distinct feature is the house's **bamboo support, thatched roof**, and integration of indoor and outdoor elements, providing a seamless flow for relaxed living.
